newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes lower, downtrend could resume.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes lower, downtrend could resume.

text.p: The gold price could take a fresh shot at getting over $380 an ounce on Thursday but that would not necessarily change the market's overriding bearish trend, dealers said.
"It is not finished with the $380 yet, but if the resistance (selling) is still in there at $380-$381.50, we may see gold moving lower later," one dealer said.
Gold was fixed at $379.50 per ounce compared with $380.30 on Wednesday afternoon and a close of $380.60.
Europe's gains on Wednesday, which took gold off 18-month lows, brought little follow-through in New York and the Far East.
"We saw some short covering and partial profit taking yesterday but there were no aggressive signs of trying to take it higher," one dealer said.
Gold began to weaken seriously last week when the mainly U.S.-based investment funds abandonded it for the higher profit potential of the stock and bond markets
All through the downtrend from last week's $383 to the recent floor at around $377, neither the Comex gold futures or the spot market had seen a day of heavy selling, dealers said.
"We could see that if it loses $380 this time," a dealer said.
A cranking up of the relatively light sales programme could take the $377-$378 floor out of consideration and introduce thoughts of $375, $370 and below, dealers and analysts said.
Physical interest remained very light and was unlikely to re-emerge until there was some assurance that gold had established a base.
Even then, it it would do no more than underpin the price. "We will not see this turned round by physical buying," a dealer said.
U.S. jobs data were due on Friday, with payrolls forecast to rise 166,000 against a 250,000 rise in August.
Unemployment was forecast at 5.2 percent for September against 5.1 percent in August.
Dealers said there was very little interest in the rest of the precious metals which were barely changed from Wednesday.
Silver was indicated at an unchanged $4.93. Platinum was steady and quiet at $384.25, 50 cents off the close. Palladium was $0.25 firmer at $121.50.
